title: PRD: Gated behavioral lanes for hosted API (chat / completions / embeddings / rerank) with acceptance & launch safety net
creator: Anya Patel
description: Purpose: Define a production PRD for introducing gated behavioral lanes across Redwood's hosted API surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Lanes are prescriptive response-quality / cost classes (e.g., fidelity tiers) that allow customers to choose tradeoffs and allow Redwood to route traffic and enforce rollbacks automatically. This PRD captures requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout and launch safety-net for the property.
scope: Implement three behavioral lanes: Fidelity-High, Fidelity-Balanced, Fidelity-Economy across chat/completions endpoints
Define embeddings lane mappings (dense vs float16 quantized embeddings) and rerank lane compatibility
Add lane metadata in endpoint contract: lane id, target latency, cost-band, deterministic flag
Telemetry + canary gates: per-lane quality evals, latency P50/P95, error rate, token cost per request
Automated rollback and fallback policies per lane (on metric breaches)
Console UI: lane selector on endpoint configuration and per-route telemetry breakdown
API: new optional param `lane` with documented semantics and SDK support (backend validates and enforces)
out_of_scope: Dedicated and Private product modes for first launch (will be included in Dedicated Q2 cadence)
Model training or model architecture changes – only serving/runtime routing/configuration
Automatic cross-region lane migration (manual routing only for rollouts)
UI for cost-estimates per-run in billing console (separate follow-up project)
requirements: API contract: `lane` query/body parameter accepted for all hosted inference endpoints; default lane is Fidelity-Balanced
Server-side enforcement: requests tagged with lane must map to runtime model variants compatible with lane constraints
Latency SLOs per lane: Fidelity-High P95 <= 550ms, Fidelity-Balanced P95 <= 350ms, Fidelity-Economy P95 <= 200ms for 16-token response baseline
Quality SLO: no more than 5% relative degradation in eval score vs baseline model for Fidelity-High; 10% for Balanced; 20% for Economy (measured on canonical eval set)
Cost metadata: per-lane estimated token cost multiplier included in telemetry and billing snapshots
Determinism contract: Fidelity-Economy must support deterministic seeding for reproducible evals where feasible
Gate metric definitions: clear thresholds for canary promotion (quality delta, latency delta, error rate, OOMs), as documented in acceptance criteria
Rollout tooling: ability to route X% of traffic to a lane or variant and ramp using traffic slices
Canary harness: automated evaluation runs vs curated prompt set on every lane-promote PR / model-change
Dashboard: per-lane KPIs (error rate, P50/P95, avg tokens, model variant used) surfaced in Console and linked from rollout UI
Operational runbook for lane breaches including notification routing to on-call, mitigation steps and rollback triggers
acceptance_criteria: API: `lane` parameter accepted by hosted chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints; SDKs return clear validation errors for unsupported lane-model combos
Contract: endpoint schema updated and published in API reference; examples for each lane provided
Performance: For a synthetic workload matching 75th percentile request size, each lane meets it's P95 latency SLO within a 10% margin in the staging perf cluster
Quality: Automated eval harness shows lane-specific quality delta vs the production baseline <= thresholds (5%/10%/20% respectively) across canonical prompt sets and customer-simulated prompts
Stability: No increase in 5xx error rate > 0.1% during a 24h canary at 5% production traffic split
Fallback: If lane promotion fails gate checks, traffic must automatically fall back to Fidelity-Balanced without dropping requests
Billing: telemetry emits per-request lane tag and cost-multiplier metric that can be joined to billing exports
Console: per-route lane selector visible in Console with explanatory copy; telemetry drilldown shows lane breakdown
Security: security review completed and KMS/HSM constraints documented for lane metadata storage
Docs: PRD approves new API docs, migration guide, and a short note for customers describing expected latency/quality tradeoffs
Chaos test: Injected GPU OOM and kernel degradation scenarios during canary does not exceed defined kill-switch thresholds before rollback completes
On-call runbook: created and validated by SRE and Product during staging cutover exercise
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Integration & SDK release: API change merged, SDKs published to canine branch, internal integration tests pass
Stage 1 - Staging canary: run 100% internal traffic; run automated eval harness; operator sign-off
Stage 2 - Small production slice: 1% external traffic for 24h; monitor KPIs; abort on any gate failures
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 15% -> 50% over multiple days with automated smoke gates and human review at 15%
Stage 4 - Global rollout: 100% opt-in availability; default remains Fidelity-Balanced for existing customers
Stage 5 - Post-launch monitoring: 14-day elevated telemetry window with weekly readout to TPM & SRE
launch_checklist: API reference and SDK docs published and linked from Console
Console UI tile for lane selector implemented and copy-reviewed by UX
Telemetry: per-request lane tag and cost multiplier validated in live telemetry pipeline
Automated eval harness: canonical prompt set and scoring pipeline in CI for lane promotions
SRE runbook and rollback automation implemented and smoke-tested
Security sign-off: security review completed and data handling for lane metadata documented
Billing integration: lane tag appears in billing exports and cost queries
Support playbook: customer-facing FAQ and escalation matrix prepared
Compliance: export controls and PII handling reviewed for lane metadata
Monitoring alerts: SLO breach alerts configured for per-lane P95 latency and error rate
Canary test: successful 24h staging canary with no gate failures
Executive readiness: launch summary and risk register reviewed by Head of Product
risks: Quality regressions in lower-fidelity lanes could see higher customer complaints if not sufficiently documented
Additional cost telemetry complexity may delay billing reconciliation for first invoice cycle
Misrouted traffic during rollout could cause unexpected latency spikes in specific regions
SDK adoption lag: customers may not pass lane param and be surprised by behavior changes (mitigate via default lane and communications)
Security/PII risk from storing lane tags in logs needs mitigation via retention and masking policies
